config.title: Memory Leak Hunt

intro.title: Memory Leak Hunt
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that simulates a memory leak scenario to understand how they occur and how to prevent them. You will learn the core concept of memory leaks in web applications, which happen when memory is allocated but not properly released, leading to performance issues. The main technologies involved are Vue's reactive state, lifecycle hooks like `onMounted` and `onUnmounted`, and event listeners. By the end, you'll practice identifying and fixing common memory leak patterns in a beginner-friendly, hands-on way.
intro.usecase: Memory leak detection is crucial in long-running Vue applications like admin dashboards or data visualization tools where users interact with dynamic charts, filters, and modals. Developers must ensure that event listeners, timers, and reactive subscriptions in components like real-time monitoring panels or complex form wizards are properly cleaned up when components unmount. Without proper cleanup, these applications gradually consume more memory, leading to sluggish performance and browser crashes during extended user sessions. Mastering memory leak prevention helps build enterprise applications that remain responsive even after hours of continuous use with multiple tab switches and component lifecycles.

objectives: Initialize reactive data properties to track memory usage in a Vue component
Implement event listeners and timers that demonstrate potential memory leak patterns
Apply Vue lifecycle hooks to properly clean up subscriptions and intervals
Construct a memory monitoring utility that logs allocation changes
Configure watchers to observe component destruction and resource release
Manipulate DOM references and event handlers to prevent orphaned connections
Integrate cleanup routines within beforeUnmount and unmounted lifecycle phases

successCriteria: The setup function contains a const memoryUsage = ref(0) declaration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Define a function to start a managed interval
steps.instruction: Define a function called 'startManagedInterval' inside the setup() function. This function should use setInterval to call allocateMemory every 1000 milliseconds, store the returned interval ID in the 'leakedIntervals' array, and log the ID to the console.
steps.hint: Use setInterval with allocateMemory as the callback, push the returned ID into leakedIntervals.value, and add a console.log statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a function that properly stores interval IDs for later cleanup, demonstrating correct memory management practices.
successCriteria: The startManagedInterval function is defined, uses setInterval with allocateMemory as callback every second, stores the interval ID in leakedIntervals, and logs the ID.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function stores the interval ID in leakedIntervals and logs it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should use setInterval to call allocateMemory every second, store the ID, and log it.

steps.expectedOutcome: The component will automatically start a managed interval when mounted and clean up all intervals when unmounted.
successCriteria: onMounted hook calls startManagedInterval, and onUnmounted hook calls cleanupIntervals.

steps.title: Build the component template with controls and display
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a heading 'Memory Leak Hunt', a paragraph that displays the current memory usage, and three buttons: one to start a leaking interval, one to start a managed interval, and one to clean up all intervals.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display reactive values in the template. Add click event handlers to buttons using @click.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example template structure template: `

Memory Leak Hunt

Memory Usage: {{ memoryUsage }}

`
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now includes a heading, memory usage display, and three interactive buttons that will trigger the corresponding functions.
successCriteria: The template contains an h2 heading with the text 'Memory Leak Hunt', a paragraph displaying 'Memory Usage: {{ memoryUsage }}', and three buttons with @click handlers for startLeakingInterval, startManagedInterval, and cleanupIntervals.
